title: Perf run 20261017-0532
heading: No speed change kept: the returning phone's cache change is parked again
meta:
The run tried the change you approved last run (ledger 0930:17): the host lets a browser keep each built file for a year, and a click on the start page takes down a preview that has loaded but not shown. On a returning phone (4× slower CPU, Fast 4G) the start page was usable after about 400 ms instead of 550 ms, called better on 5dee0a5 (550 → 393 ms, −28%, every pair 0.67–0.77). But your condition for keeping it failed on the A/B it named: the returning board showed 125 ms later (median pair ×1.23, 6 of 8 pairs slower), past your ~100 ms. Later re-checks came in under the limit, but re-measuring until a condition passes is not a fair test, so at the step 8 follow-up the change was reverted from the PR and saved as patches/assets-cache-click-0930-17.patch.

The PR now changes no app or bench code: it holds the run's record, its A/B reports and the ledger. The target, every headline row 1.2× faster than the base 5362029, was missed. The run also went well over its 4-hour budget (05:32 to about 13:00).

needs.intro: Three items. Item 1 is a trade-off for you; items 2 and 3 are information. The PR waits on none of them.

items.title: 0930:17: take the returning phone's faster start page with a later board?
items.body:
Your condition: on 8 pairs against the base, the returning phone's board at most ~100 ms later. On the A/B that tested it (ab-20261017-0532-cache.md, 5dee0a5 vs 5362029, 8 pairs) the board went 535 → 660 ms, median pair ×1.23, pairs 0.88 1.32 1.17 1.30 1.29 1.13 1.48 0.97. The change is parked, not kept. What it gives and costs, with every pair:

  • Returning phone usable: 550 → 393 ms, called better (cache A/B); −29% in the full re-check, pairs 0.67 0.84 0.70 0.60 1.00 0.66 0.74 0.54; −38% in the cold-load re-check on 0bb455f, every pair lower (0.26–0.81; that report is not committed, as it measured code the PR no longer holds).
  • Returning board: re-checks ×1.165 (1.47 1.18 0.96 1.39 0.93 0.43 1.15 1.58) and ×1.06 (0.90 1.10 1.05 1.07 1.01 1.25 0.91 1.84).
  • Returning instant first click: 40.3 → 52.8 ms, every pair slower, not called.
  • Headline rows more than 3% slower at the median pair on that code, none called. Full profile (ab-20261017-0532-final.md): reopening a long game ×1.386, pairs 0.48 1.62 0.92 2.63 0.49 1.69 2.19 1.16 (narrowed re-check ×1.098, not committed: 1.09 1.10 0.88 1.48 1.68 1.31 0.89 1.09); a shared game's page ×1.279, pairs 1.24 1.35 1.50 1.00 0.75 1.05 2.01 1.31 (narrowed ×0.98, not committed: 0.57 0.79 0.81 1.72 1.33 0.50 1.16 1.15); the player's move ×1.039, pairs 0.86 1.19 1.08 0.82 0.74 1.04 1.04 1.37. Cold-load re-check (not committed): desktop start page usable ×1.034, pairs 1.14 1.08 0.56 0.87 0.98 1.55 1.15 0.72. Cache A/B: desktop board ×1.053, pairs 1.03 0.93 1.28 1.24 0.88 1.07 0.97 1.24 (×0.985 in the full re-check). Nothing in the patch runs on a game page.

items.recommend: Leave it parked. The next run tries to win back the board first (RB1 did not), checks the click half alone (CK1) and AH3 on a Pages preview, then runs one 8-pair A/B judged by your condition as stated. Say "take it as is" if −28% on the returning start page is worth about +80–125 ms on its board.

items.title: A regression since the last run, not fixed: a picked-up piece appears about 14% later (RS1)
items.body: Since the last run's base 38d62be, "A picked-up piece appears" leans slower: ×1.10 at the median pair in the regression check (ab-20261017-0532-regress.md, 6 pairs: 1.09 1.05 1.12 1.25 0.98 1.24) and ×1.15 narrowed to the pick (ab-20261017-0532-select.md, 6 pairs: 0.93 1.14 1.26 1.15 1.23 1.15). Identical code gave ×0.98. Neither A/B calls it. A bisect found no single cause: each of #164, #163 and #167 leans +4–6.5%; none touches three/. The speed rule says to fix a regression first. It was not traced: the run's budget was spent before the Improve stage, which took your approved item first.
items.recommend: No action from you. The next run's first item: trace three picks on 38d62be and three on 5362029, then fix the cause with a called A/B or close it as drift on that evidence (ledger 1017-0532:RS1).

items.title: The 1.2× target was missed (information)
items.body: The PR keeps no code change, so the final code is the base's: ×1.0 on every headline row. With 0930:17 the full profile was ×1.001 over the 15 rows (ab-20261017-0532-final.md); only the returning phone moved. The run spent its time on the A/A and the RS1 bisect before Improve (to 08:27), then on your item and RB1; no idea for every row was tried.

scoreboard.intro:
The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Target: every one 1.2× faster than the base 5362029 (the dashed line).

The PR's final code is the base's (no code change kept), so nothing was re-measured for it. The chart below is the parked change 0930:17 on 86eb945 (the same app code as 5dee0a5): full profile, 8 pairs, ×1.001 over the 15 rows, none called; of 105 other measurements 2 called better (the returning phone's requests 18 → 2, bytes 5.3 → 0.6 KiB) and 1 worse (that visit's connection opens 410 → 481 ms).

At the start of the run, 5362029 against the last run's base 38d62be was ×0.998, none called (ab-20261017-0532-regress.md). For the long view, the last measurement against the first recorded run (92ce041) stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast over the 11 rows both can measure.

items.title: 0930:17: a returning phone keeps the built files a year; a click takes down a preview queued behind it (parked for you)
items.body: Tried as ac02f49 (the bench serves the build's own _headers) and 5dee0a5: the build writes one year-long rule per hashed file under assets/ into _headers, adds assets/404.html, and fails on an unhashed name or past the host's 100 rules (26 used); the start page's click takes down a preview whose code has arrived but not shown. Returning phone usable −28%, called better; returning board +125 ms, past your limit. Reverted at step 8, saved as patches/assets-cache-click-0930-17.patch (applies to 5362029). Its review's points stay with it in the ledger: the click half has no A/B of its own (CK1), the one-rule-per-file form nears the 100-rule ceiling with each new chunk (AH3), and the patch extends a StartScreen test that tests nothing it changes.

items.title: RB1: a returning visit asks for the preview only after the connection opens and the page is idle
items.body: Tried as 31600cf, reverted in 0b00cd8. Against 5dee0a5, cold load, 8 pairs (ab-20261017-0532-rb1.md): no headline row called. Returning usable −3.7% (5 of 8 lower), returning board −1.8% (mixed), connection open +1%. The returning first click went 58.9 → 40.7 ms, lower in every pair (0.57–0.89) but not called. Saved as patches/returning-preview-hold-RB1.patch (applies on top of the 0930:17 patch); ledger 1016-2036:RB1, parked.

choices.intro:
• 0930:17 parked at the step 8 follow-up, not kept: your condition failed on the A/B it named, and pooling the later re-checks to get under it was optional stopping. Earlier stages had kept it on all 24 pairs (×1.14, about +80 ms).
  • The bench fix ac02f49 went into the patch with it: it exists only to measure that change.
  • RS1 raised to you as information rather than traced now: the run was already about 7 hours into a 4-hour budget.
  • AH1 as one rule per built file rather than /assets/* plus a 404 page: whatever the host does with a missing name, no rule matches it (in the patch).
  • RB1 reverted under the speed rule, although its returning first click was lower in every pair.
  • The A/A, exploratory, is not committed (one line in the run record). The select narrowing is committed (ab-20261017-0532-select.md) as RS1's evidence; the RS1 bisect reports stay in bench/out/.
  • Budget: about 7.5 hours against 4 (05:32 to about 13:05).

  • RS1's cause (item 2 above).
